pluginDescription: What runs on a timer: the user's crontab and systemd's timers.
conflict: The crontab changed on the server. Reloaded.
errTitle: Could not read what is scheduled
errNoServer: This page needs a server, and none was given.
errDenied: This plugin was not given the "{0}" permission. Reinstall it to grant one.
errDeniedPlain: This plugin was not given permission for that.
errUnavailable: This host does not offer what the plugin asked for.
errTimeout: The server did not answer in time.
errIo: The server could not be reached.
errCert: The server's certificate was not the one that was reviewed.
errDecode: The answer could not be read.
emptyDetail: This account has an empty crontab. Anything another account schedules is not listed here.
emptyDetailNoTimers: This account has an empty crontab and systemd has no timers. Anything another account schedules is not listed here.
emptyNoCronDetail: The crontab command is not installed, so there is nothing to read a schedule from. systemd timers are read separately and can be turned on in settings.
prefsTimersHint: Off reads only the crontab, and asks systemd nothing
errNoCommand: A job needs a command to run.
errBadSchedule: "{0}" is not a schedule crontab will run. Five fields, or @daily and its neighbours.
fleetEmptyDetail: Add a server and this lists what runs on a timer on each of them.
